subject: Urgent: FinAlpha production errors — apparent rate-cap misalignment
messages:
From: Teresa Liu <t.liu@finalpha.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing elevated error rates and large latency spikes this morning across several of our critical routes. Our SREs report 5–8% 429s and p99 latency creeping to ~1.2s (previously ~180ms). The errors began around 08:45 PT and have affected checkout and real-time pricing calls.

Attached: finalpha_error_logs_20270504.txt (sanitized).

Can Redwood confirm whether anything changed on your side (rate limits, quota burst, routing)? This is impacting our customers and we need a timeline for mitigation.

Thanks,
Teresa
Director, Platform Reliability — FinAlpha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

Team — forwarding FinAlpha. Teresa attached logs; they see 429s and p99 jump. They asked specifically whether rate limiting or burst config changed. Can we triage? Please advise immediate mitigations and a short message I can send back. I can request credit/time window after we understand root cause.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 9:23 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding FinAlpha. Teresa attached logs; they see 429s and p99 jump.

Thanks — I'm looking at their route mapping. Initial hypothesis: the customer was recently migrated to a new routing policy (last week) that maps to a non-dedicated pool and a stricter per-client token-bucket with a small burst window (60s). If their traffic pattern had a short high-concurrency burst, the token bucket would throttle aggressively and then induce retries that amplify p99.

Immediate actions I recommend:
- Apply a short-lived quota override for FinAlpha to restore capacity while we validate (I can push a temp override if SRE approves).
- Enable per-route fallback to a compatible model variant with higher concurrency limits for their critical routes.
- Request their team to share traffic histogram for 07:00–09:00 PT.

I need Aditya to confirm whether the quota override has been applied in the next 10–15m and whether that reduces 429s.

Markus
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:53:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 9:41 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I can push a temp override if SRE approves.

I pushed a temporary quota override (temp_quota_override_FF8421.xlsx attached) at 09:50PT to increase the per-minute token allowance and widen the burst window from 60s to 180s for the customer route. I also opened PD-6291 and linked the routing snapshot (rate_policy_snapshot_20270505.json).

Early telemetry (09:51–10:05) shows 429 rate falling to <0.5% and p99 latency improving toward 210–320ms. This suggests the token-bucket/burst window mismatch is the primary contributor.

Next: Markus and I will run a controlled rollback to reproduce and then propose a permanent config change. I'll keep you posted.

--
Aditya Rao
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Teresa Liu <t.liu@finalpha.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinAlpha Ops <ops@finalpha.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

Vanessa — thank you for the rapid response and the temporary lift. We're seeing immediate improvement in customer-facing metrics and will keep monitoring. Our security/compliance lead wants an explanation of why this config changed during our migration window; they were not told about a stricter policy mapping.

Can you provide:
1) The change log that caused us to map to the stricter policy (who/when).
2) A remediation plan so this doesn't recur (permanent policy/instrumentation.)

Teresa

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Root-cause summary and mitigation plan for FinAlpha incident

Folks — brief summary for the exec and FinAlpha: we traced the root cause to a policy misalignment during FinAlpha's routing migration on 2027-04-28. An automated rollout assigned them to the "shared-economy-v2" routing tier which uses a conservative per-client token bucket (burst=60s, refill=100 tokens/min) due to historic noisy neighbors. The migration script failed to preserve the customer-level override that had been present on their previous mapping.

Impact: short high-concurrency bursts in FinAlpha's workload triggered immediate throttling, producing retries and amplifying p99. The temp override we applied reduced 429s and restored p99 near baseline.

Permanent remediation (plan):
- Immediate (24h): Create a targeted customer-level policy that mirrors their previous override (burst=180s, higher refill).
- Short term (7d): Add a migration safety check to the rollout pipeline that warns if a customer-level override will be dropped.
- Medium term (30d): Add pre-migration simulation to the routing service to predict throttle risk for identified customers and block unsafe rollouts.
- Communication: We'll provide FinAlpha a change log entry and the remediation timeline. Priyom, please prepare a short customer-facing statement (compliance-friendly) describing what happened and what we'll do to prevent recurrence.

I'll schedule a 30-min postmortem with SRE and Product tomorrow; invite to Vanessa and FinAlpha as appropriate.

Markus

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Teresa Liu <t.liu@finalpha.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — 429s and 1.2s p99 latency since 08:45PT

Teresa — thanks again for your patience. Summary of next steps we committed to:
1) We applied a targeted customer-level policy today that restores the previous burst/refill profile. This is live and we've seen stable telemetry.
2) We'll share a concise change log showing the 2027-04-28 migration details and the specific automated rollout that removed the override (link below).
3) Short-term safety: migration pipeline patch to block override drops (ETA 7 days).
4) Medium-term: pre-migration simulation and automated risk checks (ETA 30 days).

Priyom will share the customer-facing compliance statement by EOD tomorrow. Neha, I'll coordinate a 30-min review with your CS team to ensure FinAlpha walks through the postmortem.

If you want an exec-level call with our CTO and FinAlpha's head of engineering, happy to set that up; otherwise we can keep this lightweight.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: finalpha_error_logs_20270504.txt, temp_quota_override_FF8421.xlsx, rate_policy_snapshot_20270505.json
